Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Canopy Aerospace & Defense
providers.description: Canopy Aerospace & Defense (Canopy A&D) is a vertically integrated advanced materials platform serving the aerospace, defense, space, maritime, and power-electronics industries. The company manufactures and delivers highly specialized materials with exceptional insulative, absorptive, and signal-reducing characteristics, including thermal protection systems (TPS), ultra-high-temperature ceramics, additive-manufactured ceramic components, multi-layer insulation and soft goods, and composite structures. Formed by Trive Capital through the combination of Canopy Aerospace, Hera Technologies, and MSM Industries, Canopy partners with OEMs from initial design and R&D through turnkey manufacturing and refurbishment of reusable platforms, operating facilities across the US, UK, and Netherlands. This is a physical materials manufacturer and publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its web and identity surface.

providers.name: LanzaJet
providers.description: LanzaJet is a sustainable fuels technology company, headquartered at 520 Lake Cook Road, Deerfield, Illinois, that produces and licenses sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and renewable diesel. Founded in 2020 as a spin-out of LanzaTech with Suncor and Mitsui, and later backed by Shell, British Airways, Southwest Airlines, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, Breakthrough Energy, Groupe ADP, MUFG and All Nippon Airways, the company commercializes a patented Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) process that converts ethanol into synthetic paraffinic kerosene through a continuous catalytic reaction, reaching roughly 90% hydrocarbon selectivity to jet fuel and converting about 98% of the ethanol carbon into salable product. The ATJ pathway was approved by ASTM International in 2018. LanzaJet Freedom Pines Fuels in Soperton, Georgia — opened in 2024 — is the world's first commercial ethanol-to-jet SAF plant, producing roughly 10 million gallons of SAF and renewable diesel a year, and the company is developing Project Speedbird in the UK alongside a CirculAir joint solution with LanzaTech that widens the feedstock base to municipal solid waste, agricultural residues and industrial off-gases via gas fermentation. LanzaJet sells technology licenses, project development and engineering services and fuel offtake rather than software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and every /.well-known/ discovery probe against its web host returned 404.

providers.name: World View
providers.description: World View (World View Enterprises) is a Tucson, Arizona-based stratospheric balloon company focused on remote sensing and persistent intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Its uncrewed high-altitude balloons carry EO/FMV, IR, SAR, and hyperspectral sensors for defense, government, and commercial missions. Acquired by Ondas Holdings in 2026, it now operates as part of the Ondas Sentinel multi-domain intelligence platform, with partnerships including Palantir and Sierra Nevada Corporation. World View publishes no public developer program or API.

providers.name: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings
providers.description: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings is a global airfreight, charter, and aircraft leasing group headquartered in Purchase, New York and operating across more than 80 countries and 330+ airports. The holding company positions itself as the "Leader in Aviation Outsourcing" and runs three operating businesses: Atlas Air (ACMI, CMI, charter, and military/government cargo and passenger operations on Boeing 747-400F, 747-8F, 777F, 767, and 737-800BCF freighters), Polar Air Cargo (scheduled airport-to-airport cargo network, historically a joint venture with DHL), and Titan Aviation Leasing (commercial aircraft acquisition, leasing, and sale-leaseback services). Atlas is the largest operator of the Boeing 747 freighter, the Dreamlifter operator for Boeing, and one of the principal lift providers for Amazon Air's middle-mile network. In August 2022 a consortium led by Apollo Global Management with J.F. Lehman & Company and Hill City Capital agreed to take the company private in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately US$5.2 billion; the deal closed in March 2023, delisting the company (formerly Nasdaq: AAWW). As a freight carrier the group does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs — integrations with shippers, forwarders, and customers are delivered through private B2B channels (EDI, Cargo-IMP/XML messaging, airwaybill tracking on polaraircargo.com, and account-managed connectivity). A "Track Shipment" tool and a Special Loads request form (specialloads.atlasair.com) are the principal self-service surfaces; an internal-facing GitHub organization (Atlas-Air-Data-Platform) exists but publishes no public repos.

providers.name: CesiumAstro
providers.description: CesiumAstro designs, manufactures, and tests full-stack communication systems and satellites for space, air, and ground missions. The Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, builds active phased array payloads (Vireo), software-defined radios (SDR-1001/2051/2104/3104), reconfigurable processing units, SATCOM terminals (Skylark), tactical ISR/PNT payloads (Nightingale), and the integrated Element LEO satellite platform. Its hardware enables inter-satellite links, high-speed downlinks, lunar communications, and 5G non-terrestrial networks. CesiumAstro publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company as an aerospace hardware provider in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EnduroSat
providers.description: EnduroSat is a Sofia, Bulgaria-based satellite manufacturer and space service provider working to make space universally accessible by lowering the cost and complexity of accessing space data. The company builds CubeSat and SmallSat platforms (FRAME Max, FRAME L, FRAME S buses and 8U/12U/16U CubeSats), avionics and communication modules (X-Band SDR, S-Band and UHF transceivers, EPS power modules, solar panels, and antennas), and delivers end-to-end Space Service, SpaceOps, and SpaceDev offerings that take customers from idea to orbit in roughly six months. EnduroSat has deployed 100+ satellites with 3,500+ modules in operation, downlinked 500+ TB of data, and serves ~450 customers including NASA, ESA, and IBM Space. It maintains an open-source GitHub organization publishing Cubesat Space Protocol (CSP) implementations and NextGen ground-station and onboard API frameworks. Backed by Founders Fund and GV.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Isar Aerospace
providers.description: Isar Aerospace is a European space launch service provider founded in 2018 and headquartered in Ottobrunn near Munich, Germany. The company designs and manufactures Spectrum, a two-stage orbital small-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying up to 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit or up to 700 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit, using liquid oxygen and propane propulsion. Spectrum is fully developed and produced in-house with automated, scalable manufacturing including additive manufacturing and carbon-composite structures. Isar Aerospace offers dedicated, lead, and rideshare launch services for small and medium satellites and constellations. Backed by more than EUR 500 million in private capital from investors including Earlybird and HV Capital, the company employs over 400 people from nearly 50 nations and conducted the inaugural Spectrum test flight from Andoya Spaceport, Norway, on 30 March 2025.

providers.name: Morpheus Space
providers.description: Morpheus Space is an in-space mobility company building electric propulsion systems and mission-design software for the New Space economy. Founded in 2018 out of the Technical University of Dresden, its second-generation GO-2 system uses FEEP (Field Emission Electric Propulsion) technology to deliver continuous, chemical-free thrust for satellite constellation deployment, station keeping, collision avoidance, repositioning, and deorbiting. The company also offers Journey, a mission simulation and design platform that matches simulated requirements to available satellite subsystems. Morpheus Space markets ITAR-free solutions and is backed by investors including Techstars, Alpine Space Ventures, Airbus Ventures, Lavrock Ventures, and In-Q-Tel. The company publishes no public developer API; its only machine-facing surface is a platform-hosted (Wix) site MCP endpoint and an auto-generated llms.txt for agent access to public marketing content.

providers.name: 1001 AI
providers.description: 1001 (also known as 1001 AI) is a deeptech artificial intelligence company founded in 2025 by Bilal Abu-Ghazaleh, a former director of generative AI operations at Scale AI, and headquartered between London and Dubai. The company builds sovereign AI operating systems for critical infrastructure — live operational models that help operators across aviation and airports, ports and logistics, energy and grids, construction, and manufacturing predict issues, automate and optimize decisions, and improve operational efficiency, while retaining full local ownership and governance of their AI systems. Focused primarily on the GCC and wider MENA region, 1001 raised a $9 million seed round in October 2025 led by CIV, General Catalyst, and Lux Capital, followed by a $30 million Series A in June 2026 led by Lux Capital with Sanabil Investments, 9Yards, and Hanabi joining and existing backers General Catalyst, CIV, and Stanford AI researcher Chris Ré increasing their commitments. As of this profile, 1001 publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK; this entry captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Astrobotic
providers.description: Astrobotic Technology is a Pittsburgh-based space robotics company building lunar landers, rovers, and lunar surface infrastructure for NASA and commercial customers. Its product lines include the Peregrine and Griffin lunar landers, the CubeRover and Polaris rover families, LunaGrid lunar surface power, the Xodiac reusable suborbital rocket lander test platform, and spacecraft navigation, machine vision and computing systems. The company sells payload delivery to the Moon under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program, alongside the consumer MoonBox service. Voyager Technologies completed its acquisition of Astrobotic on 13 July 2026 and the business now operates as Voyager Lunar Systems from its Pittsburgh headquarters. Astrobotic sells missions and hardware, not software: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Boom
providers.description: Boom Supersonic is a Colorado-based aerospace company building Overture, a Mach 1.7 supersonic airliner designed to carry 64-80 passengers on transoceanic routes, powered by the company's Symphony engine and assembled at its Superfactory in Greensboro, North Carolina. Its XB-1 demonstrator flew supersonic in early 2025. Boom was surfaced as a portfolio company of SV Angel and added to the API Evangelist network. Boom publishes a corporate and investor-facing web presence (newsroom, careers, privacy, terms) but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, well-known discovery, or MCP surface, so no API artifacts are available to enrich; this profile captures its verifiable web and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Boom Supersonic
providers.description: Boom Supersonic is a Denver-based aerospace company building supersonic commercial aircraft to make the world dramatically more accessible. Its flagship airliner, Overture, is designed to carry passengers at twice the speed of today's jets and has orders and pre-orders from United Airlines, American Airlines, and Japan Airlines. The company develops the Symphony medium-bypass turbofan engine purpose-built for supersonic flight, flew the XB-1 demonstrator past Mach 1, and is applying its propulsion technology to Superpower gas turbines for data-center energy. Boom is a deep-tech, hardware-first manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its identity and security posture in the API Evangelist network. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric Capital, and Homebrew.

providers.name: PierSight Space
providers.description: PierSight Space is an India-based space technology company building a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites for persistent, all-weather maritime surveillance of the world's oceans. Founded by former ISRO engineer Gaurav Seth, PierSight delivers near-real-time ocean monitoring (targeting ~30-minute data latency and 100% ocean coverage) to detect illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, monitor oil spills, protect Exclusive Economic Zones, support maritime insurance risk assessment, and improve shipping operations. The company has raised roughly $8M from investors including Alpha Wave Ventures, Elevation Capital, and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass PierSight sells data solutions to enterprise and government clients and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Renoster Systems
providers.description: Renoster Systems is a carbon-credit ratings agency bringing deep transparency to the nature-based voluntary carbon markets. Using remote sensing, LiDAR, satellite data, and machine learning, Renoster independently rates forestry and other nature-based carbon offset projects, quantifying how much CO2 per credit a project has actually sequestered, and publishes public tools such as its Mercury project database and Renoster/Mercury rubric for researchers, reserve managers, policymakers, and corporate buyers. Renoster is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface; this record captures its company identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Sarla Aviation
providers.description: Sarla Aviation is an Indian advanced air mobility company building electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for urban transportation. Its flagship flying taxi, Shunya, uses a hybrid-electric propulsion system (seven electric units, dual battery packs, and a sustainable aviation fuel tank) to reach up to 250 km/h with a range up to 800 km and 150 km fully electric, in cabin configurations spanning 6-seat, 4-seat, cargo, and ambulance variants. Founded by former Lilium engineers Rakesh Gaonkar and Adrian Schmidt, the company is a portfolio company of Accel. The public website exposes no developer, API, or technical integration surface as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures corporate identity, legal, and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company (TEC) is a European deep-tech space startup founded in July 2021 by Hélène Huby and a team of aerospace engineers from Airbus and ArianeGroup. Headquartered in Munich, Germany with sites in Bordeaux, Oberpfaffenhofen, Italy, France, Houston, and the MENA region, TEC develops Nyx, a family of modular, reusable, in-orbit refuelable spacecraft designed to carry cargo — and eventually humans — to low Earth orbit, lunar orbit, and the Moon, serving space stations and long-distance research missions. The company has raised a €40.5M Series A and a €150M Series B and is a certified B Corp. It exposes no public developer API; interfaces are provided to payload customers via a Payload User's Guide.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

providers.name: ABL Space Systems
providers.description: ABL Space Systems is an American launch vehicle company founded in 2017 by Harry O'Hanley and Dan Piemont, headquartered in El Segundo, California, with operations at the Port of Long Beach, Mojave and Kodiak, Alaska. ABL built RS1, a two-stage, kerosene/liquid-oxygen small satellite launch vehicle designed to deliver 1,350 kg to low Earth orbit and 1,000 kg to sun-synchronous orbit, powered by nine in-house additively manufactured E2 engines on the first stage and one on the second. Its companion GS0 ground system packages an entire orbital launch site into standard shipping containers so a pad can be activated anywhere with a flat concrete surface and moved by land, sea or air. RS1 attempted its first orbital flight from Pacific Spaceport Complex Kodiak in January 2023 and was lost shortly after liftoff; a second vehicle was destroyed during preflight static-fire testing in July 2024. In November 2024 the company announced its exit from the commercial orbital launch market, and in February 2025 it rebranded as Long Wall, refocusing on containerized missile defense — the Cyclops exoatmospheric interceptor, RSX low-cost liquid boosters for flight testing and threat replication, and the Ironwood ground support equipment line. ABL/Long Wall is an aerospace and defense hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer API, SDK, machine-readable API contract or developer portal.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Sierra Space
providers.description: Sierra Space is a commercial space and defense technology company headquartered in Louisville, Colorado, spun out of Sierra Nevada Corporation as an independent entity in April 2021 and building on more than three decades of spaceflight heritage. The company designs and manufactures the Dream Chaser reusable lifting-body spaceplane and Shooting Star cargo module, the LIFE expandable space habitat and the Orbital Reef commercial space station developed with Blue Origin, Eclipse-class satellites for national security and on-orbit servicing missions, VORTEX rocket propulsion and hypersonics, space solar arrays and electrical power systems, environmental control and life support systems, and a broad spaceflight hardware catalog spanning valves, regulators, radiators, sensors, actuators, docking and berthing systems, deployable structures and launch adapters. Sierra Space states it has delivered more than 4,000 space systems, subsystems and components across more than 500 space missions. It is a hardware and mission-systems manufacturer rather than a software platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Fetcherr
providers.description: Fetcherr is an Israel-based AI technology company (founded 2019, Netanya) building generative-AI decision systems for the aviation industry. Its core is the Large Market Model (LMM), a generative model trained on internal airline data plus external signals (competitor prices, demand, weather, events, economic indicators) to forecast markets and drive real-time business decisions. Fetcherr productizes the LMM as a Generative Pricing Engine (GPE) for dynamic airline pricing and as ALPHA, a cloud-based retailing and inventory-management platform that integrates with existing airline PSS and legacy infrastructure. Customers include Delta, Virgin Atlantic, WestJet, Azul, and Viva Aerobus. Fetcherr is an enterprise B2B vendor and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or self-serve credentials; integration is delivered directly to airline customers. Added to the API Evangelist network as a battery-ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Sylvera
providers.description: Sylvera is a London-headquartered carbon data and climate intelligence platform — often described as the "Moody's for the voluntary carbon market" — providing independent ratings, market data, and geospatial analytics that help corporate buyers, investors, project developers, governments, and standards bodies make informed decisions across carbon and commodities markets. Founded in 2020 by Allister Furey and Samuel Gill, Sylvera combines remote sensing, machine learning over satellite imagery and LiDAR-derived biomass data, and on-the-ground project assessment to produce letter-graded ratings (e.g., AA, A, B) for carbon credit projects across nature-based (REDD+, ARR, IFM), engineered removals, renewable energy, and cookstove methodologies. The platform's product surface spans Ratings, Market Intelligence (supply, demand, and pricing signals), an Article 6 & CORSIA Hub for compliance risk, a Market Gateway to roughly 400 million tonnes of project inventory, Earth Analytics and a Biomass Atlas for geospatial MRV, and Commodity Insights covering CORSIA, LCFS, CFR, and FuelEU Maritime mechanism eligibility and carbon intensity assessments. Sylvera distributes its data through a web platform, downloadable reports, and a gated Carbon Credit Analytics API (base URL https://api.sylvera.com/v1, JSON API style, API-key auth) used to syndicate ratings and pricing into ESG and sustainability reporting tools such as Workiva, Persefoni, and Watershed. Commercial packaging runs Freemium, Essentials, and Enterprise tiers, with Accelerated Ratings, Market Forecasts, and Geospatial add-ons all sold via contact-sales; there is no public OpenAPI specification, no published SDK, and no Sylvera GitHub organization — the API and full ratings catalog are available only to authenticated enterprise customers.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Skylo
providers.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

providers.name: AAR Corp
providers.description: AAR Corp is a global aerospace and defense aftermarket solutions company and the number one aviation maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) provider in North America. They offer aircraft parts supply, airframe and component MRO, integrated software solutions (Trax, Aerostrat, Airinmar), and expeditionary services to commercial airlines and government customers worldwide.

providers.name: TrustPoint
providers.description: TrustPoint, Inc. is a space technology company building a fully commercial, next-generation global navigation satellite system (GNSS) — a C-band LEO microsatellite constellation delivering secure positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) independent of GPS, with improved accuracy, faster time to first fix, and anti-jamming / anti-spoofing capabilities for automotive, aviation, critical infrastructure, and national security applications. Headquartered in Northern Virginia with an office in Mountain View, California, and backed by DCVC, TrustPoint does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Cognitive Space
providers.description: Cognitive Space is an aerospace software company delivering AI-powered automated satellite operations for constellation and fleet management. Its CNTIENT.Optimize platform automates mission planning, tasking, and multi-ground-station pass scheduling for satellite operators and government agencies, reporting large per-operator time savings, while CNTIENT.Earth delivers satellite Data-as-a-Service. The company integrates with customer systems via APIs and serves clients including Terran Orbital, the Space Development Agency, the Air Force Research Lab, and NOAA. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Zymbly
providers.description: Zymbly is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building a voice-first AI copilot for aircraft maintenance. Its AI agents automate the administrative half of a maintenance technician's day at airlines and MROs (maintenance, repair, and overhaul organizations): troubleshooting issues, looking up parts, retrieving technical documentation, and generating compliant paperwork so technicians can focus on the aircraft. Zymbly is a demo-led B2B product with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications at this time; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and enriched from the company's public marketing site.

providers.name: Hermeus
providers.description: Hermeus is an American aerospace and defense company building rapidly reusable high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft for national-security missions in partnership with the U.S. Department of Defense. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, the company applies a hardware-rich, rapid design-build-test approach to move quickly from concept to flight. Its programs include Quarterhorse, a reusable high-speed flight-test aircraft; Darkhorse, a multi-mission reusable hypersonic uncrewed aerial system (UAS); and Chimera, a hybrid turbine-based combined-cycle engine that transitions from turbojet takeoff through supersonic flight into hypersonic acceleration. Hermeus is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile tracks the company's public web, security, and corporate properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Novo Space
providers.description: Novo Space develops high-performance, radiation-tolerant, modular electronics for the most ambitious space missions. Founded by Rodrigo Diez (CEO) and Facundo Jorge (CTO), the company builds SpaceVPX single-board computers, mass memory and GPU boards, tailored subsystems, and radiation-tolerant FPGA IP cores (SpaceWire, SpaceFibre, Ethernet/TCP-IP, CCSDS, NAND controllers, floating-point units) that let satellite and spacecraft builders reuse qualified hardware instead of re-engineering every mission. Customers and partners include Maxar, MIT, Thales Alenia Space, BAE Systems, Leonardo DRS, Mitsubishi, the US Air Force, Nvidia, Ansys, and Microchip. Novo Space is a space-computing hardware provider and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Whisper Aero
providers.description: Whisper Aero is a Crossville, Tennessee based aerospace company developing ultra-quiet electric ducted-fan propulsion that converts electricity into thrust with roughly 20 percent more efficiency and 20 dB less noise than conventional systems, scaling from 5 to 500 pounds of thrust and 40 to 400 knots for aviation, defense, and commercial applications. Backed by Kindred Ventures, Lux Capital, and Menlo Ventures. The company is a hardware manufacturer and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Textron
providers.description: Textron Inc. is a $14.8 billion Fortune 500 multi-industry company employing 34,000 people worldwide. Textron operates through five business segments: Bell (military and commercial helicopters), Textron Aviation (Cessna, Beechcraft, Hawker aircraft), Industrial (Kautex fuel systems, Textron Specialized Vehicles including E-Z-GO and Jacobsen), Textron Systems (defense and autonomous systems), and Textron Financial. As of 2026, Textron does not offer publicly documented developer APIs or integration portals.

providers.name: GE Aerospace
providers.description: A leading manufacturer of jet engines and aviation systems for commercial and military aircraft. Spun off from General Electric to focus exclusively on aerospace propulsion and services, GE Aerospace also offers software-as-a-service tooling, engine health monitoring (Collaborative Insight), TRUEngine certification, and OnPoint maintenance and support services.

providers.name: HEICO Corporation
providers.description: HEICO Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The HEICO Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Beyond Aero
providers.description: Beyond Aero is a French aerospace company building the world's first electric business aircraft powered by hydrogen propulsion. Its flagship aircraft, "One", is designed to fly more than 800 nautical miles with zero in-flight carbon emissions, targeting the light business-jet market. The company pairs rapid prototyping and iterative aircraft design with in-house engineering tools such as HADES (Hydrogen Aircraft Data Exploration Software). Backed by Initialized Capital, Beyond Aero is a frontier-tech hardware startup rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface at this time. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched with company identity and web/domain-security signals.

providers.name: Cowboy Space
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation builds space-based infrastructure for artificial-intelligence computing. Its flagship program, Stampede, is a constellation of solar-powered GPU data centers in Low Earth Orbit that integrate the rocket's upper stage with the satellite to form a megawatt-class data center with active thermal management and integrated compute. The company positions orbital compute as an alternative to terrestrial data centers, whose grid-connection lead times in major US markets can run five to seven years or more, arguing that Earth's energy grid cannot keep pace with AI demand. Cowboy Space is an early-stage aerospace and AI-infrastructure startup backed by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital; it currently publishes a corporate and careers presence with no public developer API.

providers.name: Cowboy Space Corporation
providers.description: Cowboy Space Corporation is a space infrastructure company building orbital data centers to address Earth's power constraints on artificial intelligence. Its Stampede satellite constellation places megawatt-class, GPU-equipped data centers in Low Earth Orbit powered by abundant solar energy, integrating the compute payload directly into the rocket's upper stage to maximize capacity and sidestep the multi-year terrestrial grid-connection delays that constrain traditional data centers. The company is an early-stage, venture-backed lead (backed by IVP); it currently publishes a corporate marketing site and careers portal but no developer portal, public API, or technical documentation.

providers.name: De-Ice
providers.description: De-Ice Technologies is a Somerville, Massachusetts deep-tech aviation startup building a chemical-free aircraft de-icing system that replaces conventional glycol spray with electrically heated strips applied to aircraft surfaces, removing snow and ice prior to takeoff. The technology eliminates weather-related departure delays, cuts glycol spraying costs, and reduces CO₂ emissions from idling fuel burn and chemical production. Named to Time's Best Inventions of 2024, De-Ice counts Air Canada as its launch customer and is backed by Techstars. This is a physical-hardware aviation company and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Savion Aerospace
providers.description: Savion Aerospace (FlySavion) is an aerospace company developing sustainable, zero-emissions aviation technology. Its flagship SavionJet is an autonomous blended-wing-body (ABWB) aircraft with a standup cabin and satellite-based piloting via proprietary autonomous flight software, and the company offers Zero-Emissions Flight Credits (ZFCs) as a subscription for organizations seeking carbon-free air travel beyond offsetting. Savion demonstrated a cryogenic LNG-fueled flight in 2019 and is a 500 Global (500 Startups) and Alchemist Accelerator portfolio company. The company operates as an aviation hardware and services business and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Windward
providers.description: Windward is a Maritime AI company headquartered in London and Washington D.C. delivering mission-grade, multi-source maritime intelligence for defense agencies, law enforcement, customs, energy and commodity traders, marine insurers, shippers, and financial institutions. Founded by CEO Ami Daniel, Windward fuses AIS data, remote sensing (EO, SAR, RF GEOINT), proprietary behavioral analytics, and generative AI into a single Maritime AI platform covering vessel screening, ownership and entity resolution, sanctions exposure, deceptive shipping detection, ship-to-ship transfer analysis, IUU fishing detection, smuggling detection, container tracking, and maritime infrastructure protection. Windward exposes its intelligence through the API Insights Lab, a unified GraphQL API at developer.windward.ai providing programmatic access to vessel risk scores, Organization Defined Risk (ODR), ultimate beneficial ownership, early detection signals, tracked shipments, carriers, and detention & demurrage data, along with webhooks and workflow automation. The company has no public REST/OpenAPI surface, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub org — its API is GraphQL-only with managed onboarding and expert-led implementation support.

providers.name: Esper Satellite Imagery
providers.description: Esper Satellite Imagery is an Australian space-technology company building an 18-satellite hyperspectral Earth-observation constellation (the Over The Rainbow / OTR program) to deliver global chemical-composition data of the planet's surface from orbit. Its Esperesso hyperspectral imagers capture more than 100 contiguous spectral bands spanning roughly 400 to 1000 nm, which Esper turns into mineralisation maps that identify lithium, rare earths, gold, nickel, cobalt and alteration zones for critical-mineral exploration — faster, cheaper and greener than traditional ground surveys. Founded in 2021 in Melbourne, Victoria by Iqbal and Joey Lorenczak, Esper sells custom area-of-interest mineral maps and a pre-built Northern Territory mineral map. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, security and code-repository surface.

providers.name: Jet2
providers.description: Jet2 plc (London Stock Exchange: JET2, formerly Dart Group plc) is a British leisure travel group headquartered at Low Fare Finder House, Leeds Bradford Airport, Yeadon, Leeds, West Yorkshire — an address confirmed verbatim in the Extended Validation TLS certificate served by www.jet2.com, issued to "JET2.COM LIMITED", company serial number 02739537, jurisdiction GB. Its home market is the United Kingdom. The group combines two businesses that are unusual in this sector for being deliberately fused: Jet2.com (IATA code LS, ICAO code EXS), the UK's third-largest airline, and Jet2holidays, the UK's largest ATOL holder and leading provider of ATOL-protected package holidays to the Mediterranean, the Canary Islands and European city destinations. For the year ended 31 March 2026 the group reported revenue of £7,482.1 million, operating profit of £439.6 million and a record 20.83 million passengers, flying from 14 UK airport bases including newly added London Luton and London Gatwick, with more than 63% of flown passengers buying an end-to-end package holiday and 155 Airbus A321neo aircraft on order. Jet2holidays sells through its own website and through more than 2,500 independent UK travel agent partners, and carries ABTA number Y1256. Where Jet2 sits in the distribution chain is the point of this record. Like easyJet and Ryanair, Jet2.com was built with no Global Distribution System dependency at all: it never filed fares into the GDS rail that Amadeus, Sabre and Travelport have intermediated for forty years, and it therefore never needed IATA's New Distribution Capability as a remedy. Travelport supports Jet2 in Smartpoint only as a "Direct Payment Carrier" — its low-cost-carrier workaround — point-to-point only, no connecting flights, and with no post-booking change or cancellation possible through the GDS at all ("Requests for changes must be made directly through Jet2"). In June 2025 Jet2.com signed a distribution agreement with airline technology company Kyte, whose Kyte Direct Connect (KDC) JSON/REST API "standardises airline NDC and LCC proprietary content", opening Jet2 seats and ancillaries to travel management companies and corporate booking tools for the first time, with the same content reaching agency desktops through AirGateway. Separately, Jet2holidays operates an agency API that lets independent agents sell Jet2 packages on their own bookable websites for commission. Its API posture, stated honestly, is that Jet2 runs real production distribution APIs and publishes nothing about them. There is no developer portal — developer.jet2.com, developers.jet2.com, docs.jet2.com, apis.jet2.com, ndc.jet2.com, partner.jet2.com and trade.jet2.com all fail to resolve — no API reference, no OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract, no security.txt, no .well-known catalogue and no official GitHub organisation. api.jet2.com resolves and answers HTTP 200 with nothing but the stock Microsoft IIS 10.0 default page, 404 on every spec path probed. Access is by commercial agreement only, negotiated bilaterally or through Kyte, whose own FAQ states that "Access to airline products is controlled by each airline." This record is an honest stub: apis[] is intentionally empty because no Jet2 API is publicly documented, and listing an undocumented hostname as an API would be fabrication. The evidence, including every URL probed with its HTTP status, is in review.yml. A second enrichment pass on 28 July 2026 found the one genuinely public first-party developer surface Jet2 has, and it is not an API: the Jet2 Design System, published as two npm packages under the @jet2 scope (design tokens for seven brand themes, and a React component library containing a single Button), sourced from Jet2's private Azure DevOps organisation at jet2tfs.visualstudio.com/Jet2Digital and documented at design.jet2.com behind a Supernova login. Both packages were last published in April 2024. The same pass confirmed no /.well-known/ document on any host that answers, no security.txt, no vulnerability disclosure programme, no trust centre, no public Postman collection and no SDK in any package registry. Jet2's engineering voice, such as it is, comes from Jet2 Travel Technologies (J2TT), its in-house development centre in Pune, India, which runs a public blog with an RSS feed.

providers.name: JetZero
providers.description: JetZero is a Long Beach, California aerospace company founded in 2021 by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page to bring the blended wing body (all-wing) airframe to commercial aviation. Its flagship program is the Z4, a 250-seat, international-range jetliner the company says will burn up to 50% less fuel than comparable tube-and-wing airliners, and the Jet1 full-scale demonstrator being built with Scaled Composites in Mojave, California ahead of a first flight targeted for 2027. JetZero broke ground in 2026 on a manufacturing and final-assembly campus in Greensboro, North Carolina and is opening an engineering office in Wichita, Kansas at NIAR. It is backed by the U.S. Air Force, NASA, United Airlines, Alaska Star Ventures and a $175M Series B led by B Capital, with letters of intent from Gulf Air and Japan Airlines. JetZero is an aircraft manufacturer, not a software or data provider: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its public technical surface is a supplier registration and supplier standards program.

providers.name: Firehawk Aerospace
providers.description: Firehawk Aerospace, Inc. is a Dallas, Texas defense-technology manufacturer founded in 2019 by Ronald Jones, Will Edwards and Steve Edwards that replaces conventional rocket-propulsion production with additive manufacturing. Its proprietary 3D-printed solid rocket fuel, branded 3D-Ultra, is used to build hybrid rocket engines and solid rocket motors whose fuel-grain geometry is printed rather than cast, cutting production timelines from years to weeks while removing the handling hazards of traditional energetics. The company works under U.S. Army Applications Laboratory SBIR Phase III and U.S. Air Force Test Center contracts, has flight-tested an additively manufactured GMLRS-class analog, and is expanding manufacturing capacity in Lawton, Oklahoma and Crawford, Mississippi. Firehawk now operates publicly as Firehawk Defense (firehawkdefense.com); the firehawkaerospace.com domain 301-redirects there. It is a hardware and energetics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Varda
providers.description: Varda Space Industries is a microgravity-enabled life sciences company that processes materials in orbit and returns them to Earth. Its in-house W-Series spacecraft are free-flying orbital production satellites with reentry capability, used for in-orbit pharmaceutical crystallization for biopharma partners and as a hypersonic reentry testbed for government flight testing. Backed by Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, and Lux Capital, Varda publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Firefly Aerospace
providers.description: Firefly Aerospace is an end-to-end space transportation company building the Alpha small-lift rocket, the Eclipse (formerly MLV) medium-lift vehicle, the Blue Ghost lunar lander, and the Elytra orbital vehicle (with the Ocula lunar imaging service). Firefly sells launch, lunar delivery, and on-orbit services through sales and payload-user-guide channels; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Brumby
providers.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Impulse Space
providers.description: Impulse Space is an American aerospace company founded in 2021 by Tom Mueller, building in-space transportation and mobility infrastructure. The company designs and operates orbital transfer vehicles (OTVs) that host, maneuver, and deliver payloads across and between orbits for commercial, civil, and government customers. Its product line includes Mira, an agile spacecraft for precise payload hosting and deployment across any orbit; Helios, a high-energy kick stage capable of moving up to 4,000 kg of payload from Low Earth Orbit to Geostationary Orbit in under 24 hours; and a GEO Rideshare program offering economical access to geostationary orbit. Impulse Space is a hardware and launch-services company rather than a software API provider, and does not publish a public developer portal, API, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and Founders Fund and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: Involve Space
providers.description: Involve Space is an Italian stratospheric aerospace company building real-time Earth intelligence. It operates autonomous high-altitude balloon platforms (Stratostats) that loiter around 20 kilometers for hours, days, or weeks to deliver continuous, high-resolution Earth observation, bridging the gap between satellites, drones, and ground sensors. Its Neurostar AI flight software autonomously controls individual balloons and networks of them (LoonHive), while the CLEAR GeoAI platform turns captured imagery into geospatial insights for disaster response, infrastructure and environmental monitoring, security, and in-orbit-demonstration / payload validation. A certified B Corporation headquartered in Italy with U.S. operations at the Houston Spaceport, Involve Space is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital, CDP Venture Capital, and an EIC Accelerator grant.

providers.name: Stoke Space
providers.description: Stoke Space Technologies is an American space launch company based in Kent, Washington, founded in 2020 by a team of former Blue Origin and SpaceX engineers, led by co-founders Andy Lapsa and Tom Feldman (both ex-Blue Origin). The company is developing Nova, a medium-lift, 100% fully reusable rocket aimed at dramatically lowering the cost of access to orbit, along with its Zenith full-flow staged-combustion first-stage engine, the Andromeda second-stage engine, and a reusable metallic reentry heat shield. Stoke operates a 168,000 sq ft assembly facility and headquarters in Kent and a rocket test site near Moses Lake, Washington. Backed by Spark Capital and others, the company extended its Series D financing to $860 million in 2026. Stoke Space is a physical aerospace/hardware manufacturer and launch provider; it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Astra Space
providers.description: Astra is a commercial space company providing dedicated small satellite launch services and flight-proven electric propulsion systems. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Alameda, California, Astra sells two products: Launch Services on Rocket 4 — targeting roughly 600 kg to low Earth orbit at a weekly cadence — and the Astra Spacecraft Engine, a flight-proven Hall-effect electric propulsion system sold in single- and multi-thruster configurations for satellite constellations. Astra became the fastest privately funded U.S. company to reach orbit in 2021 and returned to private ownership in July 2024. Astra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable specification; its buyer-facing surface is a set of launch-services and spacecraft-engine inquiry forms alongside a published Rocket 4 Payload User's Guide and engine data sheet.

providers.name: Muon Space
providers.description: Muon Space is a Mountain View, California-based end-to-end space systems company that designs, builds, and operates mission-optimized satellite constellations to deliver Earth Intelligence and enable real-time compute and decision-making in space. Founded in 2021 by veterans of Skybox, NASA, and SpaceX, the company's core product is Muon Halo, an integrated technology stack composed of MuSim (constellation simulation and digital twin), MuOS (IP-based software-defined network middleware connecting space, ground, and cloud), MuCore (software-configurable instrument core), Condor (modular Condor-M and Condor-XL spacecraft platforms), and MuDash (cloud-based tasking, scheduling, and operations dashboard). Muon Space's flagship public mission is FireSat, a purpose-built wildfire detection and monitoring constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance, Google Research, and the Gordon & Betty Moore Foundation; FireSat carries a high-dynamic-range multispectral IR instrument capable of detecting 5x5 meter fires across a 1,500 km swath with a 50 m nadir ground sample distance, with revisit times targeted to twenty minutes once the full constellation is operational. The Protoflight satellite produced its first-light imagery in June 2025, with the first block of three additional satellites launching in 2026 and full operational capacity targeted for 2030. Other Muon Space missions support the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Space Force for next-generation weather monitoring, Hydrosat for thermal geospatial intelligence in climate and agriculture, and global security applications including missile-defense architecture. Muon Space's revenue model is mission contracting, spacecraft and constellation delivery, and hosted data services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of the Halo platform or FireSat data feed.

providers.name: Varda Space Industries
providers.description: Varda Space Industries is an American space manufacturing company founded in 2021 and headquartered in El Segundo, California. Varda designs, builds and flies the W-Series, a free-flying orbital production satellite paired with a hypersonic reentry capsule, so that materials can be processed in microgravity and returned to Earth. The company sells three lines of service: biopharmaceutical processing (small-molecule crystallization that gravity disrupts on Earth), a government hypersonic flight testbed that uses the capsule's Mach 25 reentry as a test article carrier, and general microgravity research flights. Varda is a hardware and manufacturing-services business rather than a software vendor: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification, and customer-facing technical interfaces are documented in a downloadable Payload User Guide PDF.

providers.name: Rolls-Royce
providers.description: Rolls-Royce plc is a British multinational aerospace and defense company manufacturing aero engines (Trent series), defense propulsion, and power systems. Rolls-Royce does not publish a public developer API. The company operates supplier portals at suppliers.rolls-royce.com and maintains a small GitHub presence with the qc-cfd open-source repository covering quantum computing for computational fluid dynamics research.

providers.name: Birdstop
providers.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Northwood Space
providers.description: Northwood Space is an El Segundo, California ground-infrastructure company for the space industry, founded in 2022 by Bridgit Mendler (CEO), Griffin Cleverly (CTO), and Shaurya Luthra. It designs and delivers rapidly deployable satellite ground stations built on electronically steerable phased-array antennas that track many satellites at once with no moving parts, paired with software ("Portal") that orchestrates every contact, automates scheduling, and moves data from spacecraft to customer. Northwood aims to turn ground infrastructure into cloud-like, on-demand global capacity for defense and commercial operators. The company's software stack is described as developer-oriented with modern APIs and integration hooks, but it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Founders Fund, Washington Harbour Partners, and Alpine Space Ventures; raised a $100M Series B and won a $50M Space Force contract in early 2026.

providers.name: B/E Aerospace
providers.description: B/E Aerospace was a manufacturer of aircraft cabin interior products and a provider of aerospace services for commercial aircraft and business jets. The company was acquired by Rockwell Collins in 2017 and subsequently merged into Collins Aerospace (a Raytheon Technologies subsidiary) in 2020. B/E Aerospace products included seating, food and beverage preparation equipment, lighting systems, and oxygen systems for commercial and business aviation.

providers.name: Ampaire
providers.description: Ampaire is a Long Beach, California electric aviation company that develops hybrid-electric propulsion systems for aircraft. Its AmpDrive powertrain retrofits and powers regional aircraft, and the company reports more than 30,000 flight miles with a stated goal of cutting fuel consumption, maintenance costs, and noise. Ampaire is backed by Techstars and has worked with partners including NASA and ARPA-E. The company currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: GATE Space
providers.description: GATE Space is an Austrian aerospace company redefining in-space mobility with high-thrust chemical propulsion systems for satellites, capsules, and landing vehicles. A TU Wien spinout founded in 2022 and backed by Techstars, the company builds the GATE Jetpack — a plug-and-play, refuelable propulsion module running on green propellants that lets satellites perform rapid orbit and attitude maneuvers with no integration effort. Its patented engines have been validated across 8,000+ hot-fire tests in atmospheric and vacuum conditions, manufactured in a European facility with a 98% local supply chain. GATE Space raised €6.3M via the EIC Accelerator and its propulsion system will fly on BeaconSat, Austria's first military satellite. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface; the profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record.

providers.name: Kela Technologies
providers.description: Kela Technologies (kela.io) is a defense technology company founded by veterans of elite Israeli intelligence units, providing a secure, open platform that enables rapid and seamless integration of commercial and military systems in service of Western defense. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 after raising $39M from Sequoia Capital, Lux Capital, and In-Q-Tel (the CIA's venture arm). Kela is building "Sovereign Sky," a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation for resilient communication and navigation independent of foreign infrastructure, and acquired cloud-management company Pelanor. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single-page marketing site with a privacy policy but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Radia
providers.description: Radia is a dual-use aerospace company founded in 2016 by MIT-trained aerospace engineer Mark Lundstrom, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado with a second operating base in Italy led by Giuseppe Giordo. After roughly seven years in stealth the company emerged in March 2024 with WindRunner, an aircraft it describes as the largest ever built: roughly ten times the cargo volume of a Boeing 777, sized to carry onshore wind turbine blades of up to about 105 metres, and designed to land on semi-prepared packed-dirt or gravel strips so that oversized cargo can be flown directly to a wind farm, a forward operating site or a disaster zone rather than trucked over highways it cannot fit on. Radia frames WindRunner as a deliberately low-novelty airframe assembled from existing certified technologies to shorten the certification path, targeting entry into service in the early 2030s across three markets: energy (delivering the very large blades that make low-wind onshore sites economic), defense (outsized-volume strategic airlift), and commercial supply-chain logistics. It has assembled an industrial ecosystem of more than twenty suppliers and technology partners including Aernnova, Leonardo, AFuzion, Atitech, Latecoere, Stirling Dynamics, Collier Aerospace and Maximus Air, and has raised roughly USD 128 million from investors including ConocoPhillips, Lauder Partners, LS Power Development and HCVC. Radia is an aircraft manufacturer and logistics operator rather than a software vendor: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its only machine-readable public surface is the Strapi headless-CMS backend at radia.com/strapi that renders its own marketing site, whose content API is permission-locked and undocumented.

providers.name: General Electric
providers.description: General Electric Company has reorganized into separate publicly traded companies: GE Aerospace, focused on jet engines and aviation systems, and GE Vernova, focused on energy and power generation. GE HealthCare was spun off in 2023. No unified public developer API portal is currently published by GE Aerospace or GE Vernova.

providers.name: Reflect Orbital
providers.description: Reflect Orbital is a space-technology company developing satellite-based infrastructure to redirect natural sunlight to precise locations on Earth. It offers a Lighting service (adjustable illumination from moonlight to full-daylight intensity, controllable via app or website with no ground infrastructure) and an Energy service (augmenting solar-farm output by directing concentrated sunlight onto photovoltaic arrays). The company plans to expand its constellation from 2 satellites in 2026 toward 50,000+ by 2035. Reflect Orbital is backed by Lux Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, pricing, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: Solestial
providers.description: Solestial is a space solar energy company developing space-stable silicon photovoltaics — radiation-hardened, ultrathin flexible silicon heterojunction solar cells and modules for spacecraft. Its products are the only solar products on the market that self-cure radiation damage at operating temperatures, offering competitive performance at lower cost than III-V multijunction solar. Solestial has flight heritage across multiple spacecraft and works with customers including NASA, Boeing, and the U.S. Space Force. This is a hardware and manufacturing company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Astro Mechanica
providers.description: Astro Mechanica is a San Francisco aerospace company, founded in 2021 by Ian Brooke, reinventing supersonic flight for a new jet age. Its flagship Duality electric combined-cycle engine is engineered to stay efficient from takeoff through Mach 3+ by reconfiguring between turbofan, turbojet, and ramjet modes using a hybrid turboelectric architecture. The company designs engines, airframes, and flight systems in-house, has been selected to develop an engine for the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, and is backed by a16z, Lowercarbon Capital, and Y Combinator. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As an aerospace hardware manufacturer, Astro Mechanica publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web and identity surface only.

providers.name: AstroForge
providers.description: AstroForge is a commercial space startup founded in 2022 and based in Huntington Beach, California, focused on asteroid mining and the in-space extraction and refining of platinum group metals and other critical minerals. Backed by Initialized Capital and a Y Combinator alum, the company designs low-cost, autonomous, replicable interplanetary spacecraft to prospect and mine near-Earth asteroids, with its DeepSpace-2 mission targeting the first commercial rendezvous with a body outside Earth's gravity well. AstroForge does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a frontier-tech lead and will be enriched further if and when a developer program appears.

providers.name: Catalyx Space
providers.description: Catalyx Space Inc. is a San Francisco based space infrastructure company building an integrated platform for deploying payloads to low Earth orbit and returning them safely to the ground. The company develops autonomous orbital labs and reusable reentry vehicles (ReX) that use origami-inspired hypersonic decelerator technology to deliver heavy-mass downmass from orbit to ocean recovery zones, positioning itself as the fastest and most affordable way to deploy experiments and manufacture in orbit. Catalyx handles end-to-end space operations including spacecraft development, payload integration, launch logistics, mission control, and recovery. Surfaced as a Techstars (and Outlander) portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company currently publishes a marketing and careers presence but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Heart Aerospace
providers.description: Heart Aerospace is a hybrid-electric aircraft manufacturer founded in 2019 and headquartered in Torrance / Los Angeles, California, working to decarbonize and lower the cost of regional air travel. The company is developing the X1, a full-scale hybrid-electric technology demonstrator, and the ES-30, a 30-seat regional production aircraft, backed by strategic airline partners including United Airlines and Air Canada and investors such as Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Lowercarbon Capital, EQT Ventures, and Y Combinator. Heart Aerospace publishes no public developer or API surface; this profile tracks the company as an API Evangelist network entry in the sustainable-transport sector.

providers.name: Orbital Arc
providers.description: Orbital Arc is a Houston-based deep-tech spacecraft propulsion startup founded in 2023 by Jonathan Huffman, building Gas-Phase Field Effect Electric Propulsion (Gas FEEP) thrusters and the RIOT Drive (Relativistic Ion Thrust Drive) for satellites and in-space transportation. Its ultra-lightweight electric thrusters use solid naphthalene fuel that sublimates at room temperature instead of noble gases, targeting high specific impulse for satellite constellations. Backed by Techstars and Capital Factory, the company completed a sub-scale physics demonstration at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (TRL 3). This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC)
providers.description: Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) is a Reston, Virginia based technology integrator that delivers mission IT, enterprise IT, engineering services, and professional services to U.S. federal civilian, defense, intelligence community, and space customers. With approximately 24,000 employees and roughly $7.3 billion in annual revenue, SAIC focuses on direct technical support and integration for government organizations, spanning CJADC2, data and AI, digital transformation, quantum technologies, cloud, cybersecurity, digital workplace, digital engineering, and systems integration. SAIC has expanded its capabilities through acquisitions including Engility (2018), Unisys Federal (2020), Halfaker (2021, DoD healthcare), Koverse (2021, secure data lake for classified environments), and Forfeiture Support Associates (2023). No public REST APIs, developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or open source GitHub organization have been identified for SAIC — its software and platforms are delivered under federal contract to government customers rather than as externally-consumable developer products.

providers.name: The Exploration Company
providers.description: The Exploration Company GmbH is a European space transportation startup building reusable space vehicles "for humanity." Its flagship program, Nyx, is a reusable capsule designed to carry cargo and, eventually, crew between Earth and low Earth orbit destinations such as commercial space stations, featuring orbital propulsion, autonomous docking, and re-entry recovery. The company is also developing Storm, a high-thrust reusable rocket engine (up to 180 tons of thrust) built through European partnerships toward a globally competitive launcher. Backed by Balderton Capital and a certified B Corp, it markets itself as one of the fastest-growing space startups in the world. The company operates a marketing and careers web presence but publishes no public developer program, API, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time. Surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network with verified identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: VXB Aerospace
providers.description: VXB Aerospace is an Australian space technology company founded in 2022 by Alexander Ryan, developing generative design software and Hall-effect plasma propulsion for the satellite market. Its platform automates the design, manufacturability analysis, multi-physics modeling and validation of complex aerospace hardware such as propulsion systems, antennas and satellite layouts, while its ZEPHYR-35 Hall-effect thruster (Argon/Krypton/Xenon) provides in-orbit mobility, refueling, servicing and de-orbiting. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio lead and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Galactic Energy
providers.description: Galactic Energy (星河动力航天 — Galactic Energy (Beijing) Space Technology Co., Ltd.) is a private Chinese commercial launch company founded on 6 February 2018 and headquartered in Beijing E-Town. It builds and flies the Ceres family of solid-propellant small-lift rockets (Ceres-1, the sea-launched Ceres-1S, and the larger 3.35 m Ceres-2) and is developing the partly reusable liquid oxygen/kerosene Pallas-1 and Pallas-2 medium-lift vehicles, the Eros vehicle, the Welkin (苍穹) CQ-series liquid propellant engines, and the Edge attitude and orbital control system. Its public web surface is a corporate marketing site at galactic-energy.cn carrying product pages, a launch plan, completed-mission history, a news feed, careers listings, a Chinese-language document centre of launch-vehicle user manuals (PDF), and an HTML launch-reservation form. Contract discovery on 2026-08-04 found no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API surface of any kind: every probe for OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, an A2A agent card, /llms.txt, robots.txt and the full /.well-known/ discovery set returned HTTP 404 on every galactic-energy.cn host, and no api./developer./docs. subdomain resolves. This profile is therefore identity and domain-security only.

providers.name: Xona Space Systems
providers.description: Xona Space Systems builds Pulsar, a commercial low-Earth-orbit (LEO) positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) satellite service designed to complement and harden GPS with centimeter-level accuracy and encrypted, jam-resistant signals usable by existing GNSS devices via software updates. The planned constellation is 258 small satellites at roughly 1,080 km altitude, with the Pulsar Verified ecosystem (receivers, simulators, test platforms) delivered through partners including Trimble, Septentrio, Topcon, Furuno, and Murata. A Craft Ventures portfolio company serving defense, agriculture, telecom, transportation, maritime, aviation, and autonomous systems. No public developer API surface was found as of July 2026.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Pachama
providers.description: Pachama is a San Francisco–based climate technology company founded in 2018 that built a satellite- and machine-learning-powered platform for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of nature-based carbon projects — including forest conservation, reforestation, afforestation, and improved forest management. Pachama combined satellite imagery, LiDAR, remote sensing, and deep-learning models to measure aboveground biomass, detect deforestation, and track project performance against verified baselines, surfacing that intelligence through an online marketplace where corporate buyers (including Microsoft, Shopify, Salesforce, Flexport.org, Mercado Libre, Boom Supersonic, and Nespresso) could discover and purchase high-integrity carbon credits. In November 2025, Pachama was acquired by Carbon Direct, and its proprietary digital MRV platform and forest-carbon science team were folded into Carbon Direct's science-backed carbon management offering; pachama.com now redirects to carbon-direct.com. Throughout its life as an independent company Pachama operated a buyer marketplace and discussed plans for a partner API to embed project selection and retirement data into third-party products, but never shipped a public, self-service developer API, SDK, or open OpenAPI specification — its GitHub organization contains only forks and archived internal tooling.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities.
